title: The evidence desk
concept: A calm, tactile review desk turns technical bid evaluation into the act of laying out source documents. Folded corners, paper clips, ruled clauses, translucent highlights and a magnifying lens make evidence handling legible without a dashboard. The evidence slot remains physically empty when a reference is absent; connecting an illustrative reference changes the action to preparing a draft. Every diagram and reference is illustrative, not performed engineering or a real vendor record. Human applicability review and final judgment remain explicit.
metaphor: Physical document leaves on an evidence desk; an empty place cannot be mistaken for a supported conclusion.
choreography: Two source leaves settle onto the desk, revealing the unresolved evidence space inside the vendor reply.
Three leaves spread into an aligned reading plane; an optical highlight crosses the same clause on each source layer.
A magnifying lens inspects the bridge to the evidence position. Missing evidence leaves the gap and asks for evidence; linked evidence fills the slot and prepares a draft.
The original sits beneath the review sheet. Either an open clarification is retained or the draft exposes applicability, interpretation and rationale checks.
The source-linked output rests inside a physical document jacket, retaining original, change and rationale while awaiting evidence or human judgment.
interaction: The supplied missing/linked choice directly changes phase 2's evidence leaf, connection, color and next action. It also carries through phases 3 and 4: missing evidence retains an open clarification; linked evidence yields only a draft for human review, with no approval stamp.
contributions: Reusable folded-paper, ruled-clause and paper-clip SVG primitives with uid-scoped shadows and a purely deterministic render function.
A semantic evidence-gap interaction that changes both the physical composition and downstream review wording.
Complete authored English/Korean translation pairs, finite pauseable motion and an informative static reduced-motion state.
limitations: All data and document fragments are illustrative; no engineering assessment, applicability decision, vendor record or performance claim is represented.
Only the binary missing/linked reference state is modeled; relevance, revisions and conflicting evidence require human review and are not simulated.
Module syntax, all ten phase/choice renders, text coverage and SVG restrictions are checked in Node; browser layout and animation rendering are reserved for the host competition review.
